title: Information security addendum and flow-down of safeguards
status_rationale: No customer agreement template, security addendum or DPA was located. Business plan section 14 states contracting principles in draft. The Secure Construction Standard and Unbound requirements describe the intended technical commitments.
target_answer: We sign a security addendum committing to specific, verifiable safeguards rather than only 'reasonable security': encryption in transit and at rest with managed keys (SEC-CRYPTO-001), phishing-resistant MFA for administrative access, deny-by-default authorization with tenant isolation (SEC-AUTH-001), logging and retention periods, vulnerability remediation timelines and secure development rules. We contractually maintain safeguards consistent with the GLBA Safeguards requirements applicable to our customers, flow equivalent obligations down to subcontractors with access to customer data, and accept termination for uncured material security breach.
intended_practice: Draft security addendum aligned to the Secure Construction Standard once adopted.
customer_statement: A security addendum with specific safeguards is planned. We expect to accept GLBA-consistent safeguard obligations and subcontractor flow-down.

title: Incident and breach notification obligations
status_rationale: No customer agreement template, security addendum or DPA was located. Business plan section 14 states contracting principles in draft. Unbound requires incident detection, communication and lessons learned (SOC2-026) and a notification event catalog (UNB-RCN-PLT-002); none operates.
target_answer: We commit to notify affected customers without undue delay and in any case within 24 hours of reasonable suspicion (not confirmation) that a security incident has affected their data or covered services, the single trigger also used in ANS-IR-004, and within the shorter of any period required by law applicable to the customer: for bank customers, as soon as possible when an incident has materially disrupted or degraded services for four hours or more (bank service provider notification rule); for SEC-regulated customers, within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach of customer information (Regulation S-P). Notices state what is known, affected data, actions taken and a contact, and are updated as facts develop. Incident clocks are computed per customer from a register of each customer's notification obligations. We bear the reasonable cost of notification, forensic investigation and credit monitoring caused by our breach.
intended_practice: Build notification obligation register and incident runbook before production.
customer_statement: Incident notification commitments, including regulatory timelines that apply to bank and SEC-regulated customers, are planned but not yet contractually offered or operated.
open_questions: Is Echelon a 'bank service provider' under the 2021 notification rule for any intended customer, given Unbound serves DAF sponsors rather than banks?

title: Limitation of liability, indemnities and ability to pay
status_rationale: No customer agreement template, security addendum or DPA was located. Business plan section 14 states contracting principles in draft. Business plan section 14.06 states a draft position on liability and risk allocation. No insurance is in place to fund liability.
target_answer: Our standard cap is the greater of fees paid in the prior 12 months or a fixed amount, with a higher super-cap for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, set no higher than the insurance limits we actually carry so the commitment is fundable. Fraud, willful misconduct and our IP infringement indemnity are uncapped or separately capped. We indemnify customers against third-party IP infringement claims, including claims arising from code produced with AI tools, and against third-party claims and regulatory penalties arising from our breach where legally insurable and permissible. Loss of or corruption of customer data caused by our breach is treated as direct damages. We disclose our insurance limits so customers can judge whether the cap is backed. Excise tax and correction costs caused by errors in deterministic compliance gates are addressed by a specific indemnity in ANS-LEG-010.
intended_practice: Set caps after insurance is placed; align with LEG-004 control.
customer_statement: Standard liability and indemnity terms are not yet set. We will align our liability caps with insurance we actually hold so commitments are backed.
residual_risks: A small company may be unable to pay a large judgment above insurance regardless of contract terms.

challenge.customer_intent: Be made whole if the vendor causes a loss.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Customer bears breach costs because the vendor's cap is low or the vendor cannot pay.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: High or uncapped liability negotiated from a startup is often illusory: without assets or insurance it cannot be collected.
challenge.legally_required: No statute sets vendor liability caps; regulations require customers to manage third-party risk, which includes contract remedies.
challenge.contractually_required: Banks and enterprises commonly require super-caps for data breach.
challenge.historical_convention: Cap at 12 months' fees with negotiated data breach super-cap of multiples of fees.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Designs that never hold funds (CNV-LEG-001) and minimize sensitive data held reduce the maximum plausible loss.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Certificates of insurance matched to contractual caps.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Caps tied to verifiable insurance plus loss-reducing architecture.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, via certificates and policy endorsements.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Insurance lapses or excludes the relevant loss; cap set above coverage.
challenge.conventional_cost: Accepting uninsured super-caps creates existential exposure for Echelon.
challenge.alternative_cost: Insurance premium: medium for a startup, order-of-magnitude judgment, not sourced.
challenge.alternative_risks: Insurance limits shared across customers (aggregate erosion).
supporting_arguments: agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain; procurement teams may insist on fixed multiples.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Customers may see insurance-linked caps as the vendor limiting its exposure.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Data protection terms: DPA, service provider terms, location, deletion and legal hold
status_rationale: No customer agreement template, security addendum or DPA was located. Business plan section 14 states contracting principles in draft. Unbound requires legal holds that reach processors (UNB-XIN-REC-001), privacy-aware retention and deletion (SOC2-032) and a published subprocessor register (UNB-XIN-SAS-011).
target_answer: We sign a DPA that meets GDPR Article 28 where EU personal data is processed and that includes CCPA service provider terms (use only for the specified business purposes, no sale or sharing, no combining with other data) for US customers. Data is hosted and supported in the United States unless the customer agrees otherwise, and any transfer uses a recognized mechanism. At termination we return data in an open format and delete it, including from backups on their normal expiry, within a stated period, and certify deletion in writing. Legal hold notices from customers suspend deletion for the identified scope and are acknowledged.
intended_practice: DPA template drafted with counsel; deletion and legal hold supported by Unbound data lifecycle design.
customer_statement: A data processing addendum, deletion certification and legal hold support are planned. Data residency commitments will be offered once hosting is selected.

title: Termination, transition assistance, assignment and subcontracting
status_rationale: No customer agreement template, security addendum or DPA was located. Business plan section 14 states contracting principles in draft. Unbound defines sponsor exit (REQ-X-061) and vendor exit responsibility (UNB-GAP-028); EU DORA requires exit strategies and termination rights for ICT services supporting critical functions.
target_answer: Customers may terminate for convenience on notice, for cause, on our change of control, on our insolvency and when directed by their regulator, without penalty in the last three cases. On any termination we provide transition assistance for up to 12 months at contracted rates, sized to the capacity Echelon or a contracted successor operator actually has (see ANS-TRM-001), including full data export, continued operation during migration and cooperation with the successor. We may not assign the agreement without consent except to a successor that assumes all obligations, with notice and a customer termination right. New subcontractors with access to customer data are notified 30 days in advance through the subprocessor register, and customers may object and terminate if the objection cannot be resolved.
customer_statement: Termination, transition assistance, assignment and subprocessor change terms are planned for the standard agreement.

title: Governing law, dispute resolution, notices and service level remedies
status_rationale: No customer agreement template, security addendum or DPA was located. Business plan section 14 states contracting principles in draft.
target_answer: We propose Indiana law and venue but accept the customer's home state law for regulated customers where counsel finds no material issue. Disputes follow executive escalation then mediation before litigation, except for injunctive relief. Legal notices go to the registered legal address and a monitored legal mailbox, with a second named recipient so that notices are received when the principal is unavailable. title: Contract terms for AI use, automated decisions and model change
status_rationale: Unbound limits AI agents to recommending and preparing, never executing reserved actions (CNV-AIO-001, UNB-AGT-002), and requires source licensing and permitted AI use to be enforced (SOC2-028). No contract language exists.
target_answer: The agreement discloses where AI systems are used in delivering the service, commits that AI agents only recommend or prepare and that consequential decisions (grant approval, payment release, fund changes) are made by authorized humans or by deterministic policies the customer's board has adopted, prohibits training on customer data (see IPR), and requires notice before changing AI model providers that process customer data. Where a customer's use falls within state or EU AI laws, we support its compliance obligations.
intended_practice: Draft AI addendum aligned to Unbound requirements.
customer_statement: AI-related contract commitments are planned. Unbound is designed so that AI agents recommend and prepare but do not execute consequential actions.

title: Allocation of excise tax and correction costs caused by platform defects (sections 4966, 4967, 4958)
status_rationale: ANS-DAF-009 promises deterministic gates against taxable distributions, prohibited benefits and excess benefit transactions, but no answer addresses who bears excise tax and correction costs if a platform defect lets one through. Liability under sections 4966, 4967 and 4958 falls on the sponsor, fund managers, donors, advisors or disqualified persons, never on Echelon by law. No contract terms or insurance exist.
target_answer: Echelon proposes a specific indemnity, outside the general liability cap, for excise taxes, correction costs and reasonable donor remediation that result from an error in its deterministic compliance gates, subject to the sponsor having adopted and followed the configured policy, sized to and funded by technology E&O insurance that Echelon actually carries, and reviewed by counsel. Echelon states plainly that the statutory liability remains with the sponsor and its managers and that the indemnity is contractual reimbursement only.
current_practice: No position, contract terms or insurance exist.
intended_practice: Have counsel draft the indemnity; obtain E&O coverage before offering it; link to ANS-LEG-004.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet offered terms on excise tax caused by platform errors. The tax liability itself stays with the sponsor and its fund managers by law; Echelon plans to propose a counsel-reviewed indemnity backed by insurance it actually holds.
residual_risks: An indemnity larger than insurance is not fundable by a small company.
Some excise taxes may be uninsurable.
